notes.problem: Diagonal moire or hatch aliasing on four of the six monitor screens is a visible render artifact. The top third is a flat black wall used as a type plate, and the window band is flat navy with no exterior.
notes.fix: Give each screen a mipmapped emissive UI texture at render resolution so the aliasing goes, and raise the camera to take in the room's ceiling lights and a dusk exterior through the glass, so the type sits on a lit wall the room actually has.

notes.problem: The screen moire is still visible on monitors 1 to 4 as diagonal stipple patterns. The ribbon window is a flat navy band with no outside, the top third is flat near-black and the bottom third is empty tile.
notes.fix: Replace the screen texture with a flat emissive plane carrying no sampled pattern (mipmapped, no shadow receive), put the rendered blue-hour lot with two lit lamp heads behind the ribbon window, and raise the camera about 0.4 m so the desk run, not bare floor, fills the lower third under the labels.

notes.problem: The top 35% of the frame is a flat black field carrying the type. The ribbon window is a flat blue band with nothing outside it, though the dossier promised lot lamps. The monitor screens show hatched moire.
notes.fix: Model the ceiling (acoustic tile grid and a line of dimmed downlights) so the type sits on a dark lit surface rather than a fill. Put the lot lamps and a sliver of the tower in the window. Replace the screens' hatched texture with a smooth emissive gradient to kill the aliasing.

notes.problem: A flat near-elevation facade with no ground and no raking light reads as a diagram, not a photograph of a place.
notes.fix: Rotate the camera about 20 degrees off-axis, low, with the sun-side edge catching dusk light, and include the base of the building at ground with contact shadow.

notes.problem: A flat CG elevation: an untextured navy facade with no ground, no contact and no grime against a plain gradient. The one gold bay is a flat orange square with no interior falloff, so the turn's focal point is the least-modelled thing in the frame.
notes.fix: Lower the long-lens camera from the garage deck so the bottom fifth of the frame is the tower's podium on a lamp-lit plaza with TXT.contact and TXT.weather streaks under the spandrels, and give the gold bay the same lit-room gradient and glass roughness as the cool bays at a warm emissive.

notes.problem: The square-on facade has almost no grade. The window fills are flat, the precast is one value, and the planned garage lip and helipad edge are missing, so the turn frame looks like a diagram of a building.
notes.fix: Rake the lamp light across the facade from the declared -60 azimuth so spandrels and mullions cast shadow down the face. Add the garage parapet's concrete lip as a dark foreground band at the bottom, and the roof parapet against the sky as planned.

notes.problem: A cropped light pool at the right edge (about x 1560, y 1580 display) has no visible source. The skyline is untextured blocks, and the lower half is a dark lot holding the type.
notes.fix: Delete or re-aim the off-frame lamp, add atmospheric haze and window lights to the skyline, and bring the lot's lamp pools up under the type so it sits on lit asphalt.

notes.problem: Cars crowd the bottom right under the url, a half light pool is clipped at the right edge (about 1540,1580), a stray dark blob sits left of the hook (about 280,1190), and the Dallas skyline is plain extruded boxes.
notes.fix: Clear the bottom-right parking rows out of the footer band, remove the clipped pool and the blob, and push the skyline further into haze with lit window grids so it reads as Dallas rather than placeholders.

notes.problem: Aerial over a flat, blotchy grey ground plane that reads as void. The Dallas skyline is cardboard extrusions. The bottom third is a dead dark field under the type (machine_qa: bottom 33% craft density).
notes.fix: Drop the camera from 40 m to about 12 m and pitch it up so the horizon sits on the upper third. Run the marked lot, with lamp pools, car contact shadows and St. Augustine islands, through the bottom third under the dek, and grade the ground into the skyline haze so the city sits in air rather than on a grey sheet.

notes.problem: A dark horizontal band behind the dek (about y 500 to 840 display) reads as a plate. The figures are low-poly toys on a featureless floor with no room around them.
notes.fix: Remove the band and build the waiting room with ceiling fixtures, a back wall and a reception desk, then set the dek in that wall's quiet. Lower the camera to seated eye height so the 13 figures read as people at true scale.

notes.problem: A dark band behind the dek with a hard bottom edge at about y 845 reads as a type plate. The new glazing opens onto plain navy, the downlights don't read, and the gold motif is missing at the turn.
notes.fix: Pull the camera back so the dek sits on the glazing, and render the lit tower with its twelve gold bays through that glazing, which removes the band. Make the downlights visible as pools on the floor between the two chair blocks.

notes.problem: The waiting room reads as a dark blue void with streaky vertical lines, and a black horizontal band behind the dek works as a type plate. The seated figures are toy-like and the room has no ceiling, light fixtures or visible glazing to the blue-hour sky the dossier promised.
notes.fix: Build the room in TXT.interior: a ceiling with a run of downlights pooling on the floor, and the lobby glazing showing the blue-hour lot in the top band. Delete the black band so the dek sits on the dark mullion wall. Lower the eye from 2.6 m to about 1.8 m so the chairs show contact shadows and the people read at human scale.

notes.problem: The lower 45 percent is a navy fall-off and the headline and dek sit in a void (machine_qa: bottom third at 28 percent craft density). The upper-left sky is a flat grey slab.
notes.fix: Drop the camera toward the drive and extend the lit apron forward: curb, ambulance-bay striping and a wet-asphalt reflection of the canopy light. The type then sits on ground, and the dusk sky gradient replaces the grey slab top left.

notes.problem: The sky is a flat grey slab and a navy fade over the lower 42% works as a type plate (machine_qa: top-loaded, bottom 28%). The floor pool is a hard white disc, and a blur halo sits behind 'ANTONIO EMERGENCY' in the kicker.
notes.fix: Tilt the camera down so the wet, lamp-lit apron and the kerb run to the bottom edge under the type (asphalt with a soft-falloff pool, not a vignette), give the sky the deck's blue-hour gradient, and move the kicker off the tower's edge or kill the backdrop blur there.

notes.problem: This is frame 1's render reused: same camera, lamps, tree and SUVs, plus one figure and a red pickup. The close does not move the deck.
notes.fix: Move the camera to the main entrance at full night, looking up the facade with the 12 gold windows lit and the figure at the door. The bookend then reads as arrival rather than a repeat.

notes.problem: The note screen is seven blocks of uniform orange bars, which reads as placeholder UI. The window is a flat blue band and the planned cropped chair back is absent, so the close crop has no depth cue in front of the subject.
notes.fix: Add the mesh chair back cropped hard at near left with a cool rim from the window. Vary the line lengths and give the bars an emissive falloff and slight bloom so they read as text at a distance. Put two lot lamps in the window as the dossier specified.

notes.problem: The lamp pools are hard-edged, near-clipped white ellipses on untextured brown ground, and a palm trunk carries a white hatched alpha artifact at about x 1100, y 1450-1530.
notes.fix: Give the pools a soft inverse-square falloff at about 60% of their current peak on a worn asphalt and sand-verge ground, and fix the palm bark's alpha so the trunk base renders solid.
